title: What to Eat After Tooth Extraction: Healing Diet Guide
seoTitle: What to Eat After a Tooth Extraction: Day by Day
seoDescription: A staged eating plan for the first two weeks after an extraction, 20 soft food ideas, and the red flags to watch. Post-op guidance from Valencia.
excerpt: A staged plan for the first two weeks after an extraction: what to eat and when, 20 soft food ideas, how to protect the clot, and when to call.
keyTakeaways: First 24 hours: room-temperature liquids, broth, yogurt and protein shakes; no hot drinks, alcohol, carbonation or straws.
Days 1 to 3: blended soups, mashed potatoes and soft eggs; days 3 to 7: soft pasta, fish and well-cooked vegetables.
The article cites AAOMS dry socket rates of about 2 to 5 percent for routine extractions, higher for impacted third molars.
Gentle salt-water rinses are usually safe after 24 hours; avoid spitting, vigorous rinsing and straws for at least 7 days.
Call if pain worsens after 48 to 72 hours, you notice pus or a foul taste, or you have fever or uncontrolled bleeding.
imageAlt: Soft foods for after a tooth extraction: smoothie, eggs, mashed sweet potato and soup
flags: Last FAQ answer ('Are there recipes for easy, nutrient-dense soft meals?') has the button text 'Schedule a Post-Op Check' appended; FAQ extraction is malformed.
Comparison table lists 'May be lower in chewing-related calorie burn' as a con of soft liquids; dubious claim.
'Bone broth or enriched soups for calories and collagen' implies a collagen benefit for healing that is not established.
Reddit anecdotes (weight loss after three extractions, 'blackened socket at day 10') are unverifiable.
'Schedule a Post-Op Check' button links to an external Weave booking URL (book2.getweave.com); confirm it is current.
'We provide recipe handouts in our postoperative packet and can email them on request' is an operational claim to confirm with the practice.
